shorts.title: A Leopard's Fangs Fit the Holes in This Ancient Skull
shorts.outro: Later, Doug dressed as the leopard's usual prey and stood very still under its tree. How that went is in the full video below.
shorts.end_card: DID THE LEOPARD FALL FOR DOUG?
shorts.description: Two holes in a 1.8-million-year-old skull matched a leopard's fangs, and what Doug tried next with that leopard is in the full episode.

shorts.title: This Ancient Crocodile's Name Means Man-Eating
shorts.outro: Doug only wanted a drink from that same lake, so he put in just one foot. That decision is in the full video below.
shorts.end_card: DID DOUG GET HIS FOOT BACK?
shorts.description: A six-meter horned crocodile left bite marks on early human foot bones, and what happened when Doug stepped into its lake is in the full episode.

shorts.title: A Giant Hyena Turned Peking Man's Cave Into Its Den
shorts.outro: Doug found that den, crouched down and said hello to a cub. He forgot who it lives with. Full video below.
shorts.end_card: WHO CAME HOME TO THE DEN?
shorts.description: Most of the Peking Man fossils carry carnivore damage from a lion-weight hyena, and who came home while Doug visited the den is in the full episode.
